rationale: The torch collector already ran and resolved attribution completely: coverage.json shows 66441/66441 CUDA kernels associated with 0 unassociated, 0 ambiguous forward sequences and 0 autograd ranges, and the source uses plain eager execution with no CUDA graphs, so no overlap, graph-tracing or attribution question remains that would justify the optional nsys run. Observations mark communication not_applicable for this single-device task (no collectives, no distributed backend), which rules out nccl_tuning, collective_calibration and any bucket/protocol/wire-bytes dimension; those are listed as unavailable with reasons rather than requested. The frozen objective (generated_tokens_per_second, with ttft_ms and decode sub-goals on batch=1, 256+32 tokens) is dominated by the host-driven decode loop in qwen_inference.py: 31 sequential single-token forward calls plus argmax between two explicit torch.cuda.synchronize boundaries. The open diagnostic questions are therefore (a) how wall time splits into GPU intervals versus idle gaps across prefill and each decode step, and where synchronization lands relative to the ttft boundary, addressed by execution_timeline's CPU-to-CUDA submit associations, synchronization events and per-device intervals, and (b) whether host dispatch and framework binding costs bound per-token latency, addressed by python_runtime's warmed cProfile call trace with inclusive/self host times, accepting that it perturbs execution and is not a performance score. device_telemetry is not selected because its device-wide NVML sampling windows cannot attribute per-step decode behavior or per-op bytes, and the per-device intervals from execution_timeline answer the idle-gap question with attribution; candidate_diagnostics is not selected because no specific candidate is in evidence to probe. GPU work stays in the leased framework worker; only CPU-side library/API inspection uses /root/autodl-tmp/dev-venv/bin/python per worker-environment.json.
